sentences.text: This matter is taken up through hybrid arrangement.

3. The Petitioner being in custody in Satyabadi P.S. Case No. 207 of 2022 corresponding to G.R.
Case No.1535 of 2022 pending in the court of learned 2nd Additional Sessions Judge, Puri ,
registered for the alleged commission of offences under Sec.452/376(2)(f)G)(i)(n)/294/506/34 of IPC read with Section 376(2)(f) (j)(i)(n) I.P.C., has filed this petition for his release on bail.
4. The prosecution case as per the FIR lodged by the informant that taking advantage of her daughter, who is physically handicapped, the Petitioner committed sexual intercourse with her.
On 10.07.2022 when the informant suddenly came from her work, she found that the Petitioner has committed rape of her daughter.
On seeing the informant, the, the Petitioner fled from the spot.
Hence, this case.
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the petitioner has no connection whatsoever with the offences alleged by the prosecution.
It is further submitted that the petitioner has been in custody since 21.07.2022.
Hence, he submits that the Petitioner may be enlarged on bail.

6. Learned counsel for the State submits that the allegations made against the Petitioner are grave and serious in nature.
Hence, he vehemently opposes the prayer for bail.

7. Considering the nature and gravity of the accusations, the character of evidence available against the Petitioner, the severity of the prescribed punishment, and the absence of reasonable grounds to believe that the petitioner is not guilty of the alleged offence or is unlikely to commit a similar offence if released, this Court finds no merit in the prayer for bail.
Accordingly, the bail application stands rejected.
8. The BLAPL is, accordingly, dismissed.
( Dr. S.K. Panigrahi) Judge Murmu Laxminarayan Behera @ Chagala vs State Of Odisha ........ Opposite ... on 9 May, 2025
